1. The frames show a grid of small blocks, like a wall or a stack of tiles. A band of darker blocks runs through it, and a small block sits off to the right. The header names the data sources: FHFA home prices, BLS rents and Freddie Mac mortgage rates. A badge says "ILLUSTRATIVE", and the footer says "US only · history, not a forecast". The idea seems to be a historical comparison of US home prices, rents and mortgage rates. Each block appears to stand for a unit of cost or value. The dark blocks seem to mark one part of the total, and I can't tell which part from the image.

2. The dark band changes from frame to frame. It moves and reshapes across the grid, and in frames 3 to 6 dark blocks build up along the left edge. The right edge of the light area also steps down in frames 1 to 3. The caption "January 1991" stays the same in all six frames. In frames 5 and 6 a label appears reading "five years: 74.4%".

3. My best reading is that the animation steps through five-year windows of US history. It shows how much some quantity changed over each window, and the 74.4% figure is the result for one of them. The image doesn't say which quantity that is: home prices, rents, total cost or something else. It also doesn't say which window the figure covers. The "January 1991" label may be the start of the series, but it doesn't change as the frames advance. The "illustrative" and "not a forecast" labels mean the picture is a schematic, not a precise chart. It shouldn't be read as a prediction.

4. I don't see any clear advice. The animation doesn't say whether to rent or buy, and it gives no totals that compare the two. The only number is 74.4% over five years, with no stated subject. It doesn't answer whether renting costs more than buying once interest, tax, insurance and repairs are counted.

5. Answer to 4: none. The animation doesn't suggest any advice, and I'm not adding any of my own.
